programmes.name: Restart Scheme

insights.title: Improvement still leaves an outcome gap
insights.evidence: England & Wales · Nov 2025–Apr 2026: 41,910 outcomes against 44,150 expected TPL outcomes, an approximate gap of 2,240. Achievement improved from 81.0% in the previous six months to 94.9%.
insights.meaning: The size of the remaining gap helps prioritise contract reviews alongside the direction of change. These are outcomes recorded in the window, not a participant employment rate or a forecast.
insights.action: Use the selected monthly counts to identify where the gap arises. Review mature cohorts, pending earnings thresholds and employer follow-up before setting the next delivery action.

insights.title: Above the minimum does not mean meeting tender expectations
insights.evidence: Programme-wide · Nov 2025–Apr 2026: DWP reports all 12 contract areas at or above MPL, but only two at or above TPL.
insights.meaning: A favourable minimum-performance ratio can coexist with a shortfall against the higher tender expectation. DWP’s published classification is retained; rounded ratios are not a contractual compliance decision.
insights.action: Put actual outcomes, the TPL gap and the MPL position together in each contract review. Escalate the delivery issue against the relevant expectation, rather than relying on one green percentage.

insights.title: Check April outcome timing before changing the delivery plan
insights.evidence: Programme-wide · statistics to Apr 2026: DWP links lower April outcome rates with the annual National Living Wage increase, which raises the cumulative earnings threshold for an outcome.
insights.meaning: An April fall may reflect when earnings reach the threshold as well as underlying delivery. The monthly chart cannot separate those effects.
insights.action: Check participant earnings progress and cohort maturity against the applicable threshold. Distinguish delayed recognition from weak job-entry or retention performance before changing staffing or employer support.

rules.title: Use mature cohorts
rules.text: Compare national 6-, 12- or 21-month outcomes only where a cohort has had the full observation window. First earnings and job outcomes have different definitions.

rules.title: Separate standards from results
rules.text: Customer Service Standards describe required delivery. No public CPA-level compliance series is included.

rules.title: Put service standards alongside outcome trends
rules.text: The version 5.03 delivery overview requires the initial diagnostic assessment and signed SMART action plan within eight weeks of referral, and one-to-one support at least every ten working days. Use your own case audit to check these requirements; public TPL and MPL results do not establish compliance.

rules.title: Interpret rounded thresholds carefully
rules.text: DWP classifies two CPAs as meeting TPL in Nov 2025–Apr 2026. Ratios calculated from rounded published counts can differ near 100%; they do not establish contractual compliance. Outcome gaps use the same scope and window on both sides.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Connected the selected six-month outcome gap or surplus to delivery review, separated minimum and tender expectations, and retained April earnings-threshold context. Statistical series are unchanged.

gaps: CPA-specific cohort outcomes and monthly starts are not available in the reviewed tables.
Customer Service Standard performance, active caseload and staffing require provider data.

programmes.name: Connect to Work
programmes.scope: England & Wales · Greater Manchester pilot excluded

insights.title: The model mix changes specialist capacity
insights.evidence: England guidance · planning illustration: 100 active participants require four IPS caseloads at 25 per specialist, or five SEQF caseloads at 20. That is 25% more specialist capacity at the published average maxima.
insights.meaning: Equal participant numbers do not imply equal staffing. This is caseload capacity, not a complete staffing establishment; England guidance also advises avoiding mixed IPS and SEQF caseloads.
insights.action: Enter active IPS and SEQF numbers separately in the capacity tool. Compare the result with available specialist time, then allow for leave, supervision and expected intake before deciding recruitment needs.

insights.title: An 87% start share is not an 87% staffing allocation
insights.evidence: National starts · Apr 2025–Jun 2026: 87% entered out-of-work support and 13% in-work retention. The published definitions allow different support durations for the two journeys.
insights.meaning: Active workload depends on time in support and contact demand as well as intake. Applying the start split directly to staffing can misstate the retention capacity needed.
insights.action: Review active participants, time in support and contact demand separately for each journey. Assign retention cover from that local workload, using the national split as context rather than a target.

insights.title: Plan for uneven intake, not a straight growth line
insights.evidence: National monthly starts · 2026: 4,200 in March, 3,100 in April and 4,300 in June. Intake recovered after April rather than increasing steadily.
insights.meaning: These rounded counts span a staggered rollout. They cannot establish demand in a particular area, but show why one month is a weak basis for a staffing forecast.
insights.action: Use a rolling local forecast of accepted referrals, expected starts and exits. Reconcile it with active caseload and available specialist capacity before bringing forward recruitment or new cohorts.

rules.title: Active means engaged
rules.text: Use participants actively engaged in the previous month, not cumulative programme starts. The calculator is a planning scenario, not a published staffing count.

rules.title: Allow outcome maturity
rules.text: Out-of-work first earnings, lower outcomes and higher outcomes are separate measures. In-work retention has a separate higher-outcome measure.

rules.title: Keep IPS and SEQF capacity distinct
rules.text: England guidance paragraphs 53–56 treats caseload limits as delivery-area averages and says mixed IPS/SEQF caseloads should be avoided. The calculator estimates direct specialist capacity only. Confirm the local model and add time for supervision, employer engagement, leave and integration with health services.

rules.title: Agree the local referral and handover route
rules.text: The accountable body determines local delivery within the grant guidance. Before accepting referrals, confirm eligibility, IPS or SEQF allocation, in-work or out-of-work journey, consent and the receiving specialist. CareerPath recommends tracking referral-to-first-contact time separately from programme starts.

rules.title: Keep early outcomes within their journey
rules.text: The cumulative counts overlap: first earnings, lower outcomes and higher outcomes must not be added or divided by all starts to infer a conversion rate. Use eligible, sufficiently mature local cohorts for each support journey.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Quantified model-specific specialist capacity, separated starts from active workload and highlighted uneven monthly intake. National rollout figures are not local staffing targets.

gaps: Comparable delivery-area outcome rates are not supplied in the reviewed release.
Local grant agreements, actual active caseloads and fidelity scores require separate evidence.

programmes.name: WorkWell

insights.title: Test employer access to a service supporting people in work
insights.evidence: Pilot MI · Oct 2024–Mar 2026, 14 reporting areas: 43% were in work at entry, but employers were the recorded referral route for 2% of starts.
insights.meaning: This makes employer access worth examining. It does not establish employer disengagement: employer signposting may appear as self-referral or another recorded route.
insights.action: Ask local employers how they direct staff to the service. Separate direct referrals from employer-prompted self-referrals and check accepted handovers before deciding whether employer outreach needs changing.

insights.title: Match health-partner capacity to the barriers presented
insights.evidence: Pilot MI · Oct 2024–Mar 2026: mental health was the self-reported primary barrier for 47% of starts and musculoskeletal conditions for 22%. Frimley is outside the published coverage.
insights.meaning: These profiles identify relevant partner services, not clinical diagnoses or current waiting-list pressure. Employment coaches should not be assumed to provide the treatment participants need.
insights.action: Review referral acceptance, waiting times and completed handovers with local mental-health and musculoskeletal services. Agree who maintains employment support while a participant waits, and resolve the limiting handover.

insights.title: Resolve the limiting handover before expanding intake
insights.evidence: Early implementation evaluation · Oct 2024–Mar 2025: pilot delivery encountered staffing, procurement and information-governance delays.
insights.meaning: More referrals cannot resolve a missing coach, an unsigned service arrangement or an incomplete information-sharing process. This is historical implementation learning, not a claim that those pilots remain delayed.
insights.action: Trace an accepted referral through the local service. Identify the step causing delay, assign an owner and confirm a workable handover before increasing the next intake.

rules.title: Separate pilot and expansion
rules.text: Keep the October 2024–March 2026 pilot series distinct from national expansion. Avoid treating expansion funding as pilot expenditure.

rules.title: Make the handover visible
rules.text: The evaluation describes uneven integration between health and employment partners. CareerPath recommends recording the referral route, named owner, next contact and handover outcome, with an escalation route for delayed or declined referrals. Keep this operational review separate from the published pilot starts table.

rules.title: Read pilot volumes as scale, not impact
rules.text: Starts and participant profiles cover 14 of 15 pilot sites in Oct 2024–Mar 2026. Launch dates and populations differ. No complete referral denominator or comparable employment/health outcomes are supplied; September workload cannot be inferred.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Added employer-access and health-partner capacity findings, with dated mobilisation learning. The pilot profile is not a current caseload or an impact estimate.

gaps: No published employment or health outcomes in this pilot release.
Frimley is missing, not zero; area starts are not adjusted for population or launch date.
Early implementation learning is included, but a longitudinal causal impact estimate is not available in the reviewed evaluation.

programmes.name: Skills Bootcamps

insights.title: Completion leaves a substantial progression task
insights.evidence: England · historical 2023/24 benchmark: 43,020 completed and 28,360 had a recorded positive outcome. Approximately 14,660 completers, or 34.1%, had no recorded positive outcome.
insights.meaning: This locates a task after training, but does not mean those learners were unemployed. Positive outcomes include progression and self-employment as well as new jobs.
insights.action: Separate completers awaiting progression from cases with missing evidence or incomplete follow-up. Use that split to decide whether employer engagement, learner support or evidence collection needs attention.

insights.title: Digital needs its own progression benchmark
insights.evidence: England · historical 2023/24 sector context: 47% of Digital completers had a positive outcome, compared with 83% in Construction.
insights.meaning: The difference makes a single national progression target a weak comparator for a mixed offer. These unadjusted sector rates do not establish provider quality or justify switching provision.
insights.action: Use your sector’s completion and outcomes-per-completion figures in the table to locate the gap. Examine employer fit and follow-up for that provision; the separate region table is not a sector-by-region comparison.

insights.title: Employment-entry mix changes the relevant comparison
insights.evidence: England · historical 2023/24 benchmark: learners not in paid employment had a 35% outcome rate, compared with 47% across all starts.
insights.meaning: An offer focused on job entry should not be judged only against a total that also includes existing employees and self-employed learners. The comparison is not adjusted for learner or course mix.
insights.action: Split your delivery review by employment status at entry. Compare like outcomes and follow-up periods, then investigate where the job-entry group needs stronger vacancy matching or progression support.

rules.title: Protect milestone evidence
rules.text: For relevant non-HGV DPS 1/2 contracts, milestones are 40% start, 30% completion and 30% outcome. Wave 3 and HGV differ. Check the applicable contract.

rules.title: Record the correct event
rules.text: New starts from August 2025 use event indicators. Outcome dates and completion dates have distinct roles in payment.

rules.title: Check completion before claiming the milestone
rules.text: For non-HGV provision, the technical guide requires the qualifying period, completed subject learning and an eligible completion event or achieved outcome. A course end date alone is insufficient. For starts from 1 August 2025, record the applicable event indicator and event date; keep pre-August starts on the earlier event-aim method.

rules.title: Reconcile the contract and outcome dates
rules.text: Check the ILR contract reference against the funder agreement and the last eligible milestone date. An outcome payment needs an eligible outcome, achievement date, outcome code 1 and completed programme record. The 2023/24 benchmark is historical and is not a 2026/27 contractual target.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Quantified the post-completion progression gap and distinguished sector and employment-entry benchmarks. All comparisons remain clearly labelled as historical 2023/24 evidence.

gaps: The benchmark is financial year 2023/24. All published sector groups and regions are shown separately; this is not a combined sector-by-region comparison.
Named-provider performance is not in these tables. Different learner and course mixes affect comparisons. Financial allocations do not show delivery performance.

kpis.label: Starts growth
kpis.note: Same nine months a year earlier

insights.title: Give withdrawals a separate review from assessment results
insights.evidence: England QAR · 2023/24 to 2024/25: retention increased by 4.8 percentage points, while the pass rate increased by 0.4 points.
insights.meaning: The larger national movement was in retention. An assessment-focused response alone may miss a local withdrawal issue; these national changes do not explain why an individual provider’s QAR changed.
insights.action: Find the standards and employers contributing the largest withdrawal counts. Review when learners leave and the recorded reasons, then decide whether onboarding, employer support or in-learning intervention needs changing.

insights.title: Overall provider QAR can conceal provision mix
insights.evidence: England · 2024/25 QAR: Construction recorded 58.3%, compared with 74.8% in Education and Training. The overall national rate was 65.4%.
insights.meaning: A provider-wide difference can reflect the provision delivered as well as performance. The provider-overall and national-standard tables here are separate, unadjusted evidence.
insights.action: Examine the relevant standard, level and leaver volume before escalating an overall rate. Use your own provider-by-standard results for a matched review; do not manufacture that comparison by joining the two public tables.

insights.title: Employer funding status changes the contribution for adult starts
insights.evidence: England · applicable starts from 1 Aug 2026 aged 25+: where a levy payer has insufficient account funds, government funds 75% of eligible training and assessment costs within the band limit. Non-levy employer co-investment remains 5%.
insights.meaning: The employer contribution can differ materially for the same apprenticeship. The version 3 rules also contain age and eligibility exceptions; one standard contribution quote can be wrong.
insights.action: Confirm start date, age, employer levy status, available funds, band limit and exceptions before quoting. Check the complete funding rules and record the basis of the employer’s contribution.

rules.title: Apply rules by start date
rules.text: Use the funding-rule version applicable to each apprenticeship start, including changes to co-investment and assessment.

rules.title: Read QAR on its own basis
rules.text: Use the hybrid end year and published rate. No data, unavailable and suppressed cells must not be converted to zero. Use leaver counts to judge scale, not to recalculate the published rate.

rules.title: Recheck employer quotes for August 2026 starts
rules.text: Version 3 confirms 75% government funding for new starts aged 25+ where a levy payer has insufficient account funds; non-levy employers normally contribute 5% for that age group. Eligible 16–24 starts are fully funded up to the band maximum in both cases. Check age at start, employer status, account funds and exceptions before quoting.

rules.title: Agree assessment responsibilities early
rules.text: For revised assessment plans, engage the assessment organisation at the start and agree each party’s role and price. The rules distinguish gateway to completion from assessment during the programme. A change in the training/assessment price split needs employer approval when the total price increases; check the applicable effective date.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Strengthened withdrawal and provision-mix decisions and surfaced the August 2026 employer co-investment distinction. Historical QAR and current funding rules remain separate.

gaps: Provider comparisons are overall QAR, not adjusted for provision or learner mix. National standard benchmarks are separate, not a provider-by-standard comparison.
Unavailable or suppressed values remain explicit. Rounded leaver counts are not exact denominators for recalculating QAR. Provider identities cover any of the three years, not only current delivery.

programmes.name: Adult Skills Fund

insights.title: Measure the eligible-delivery gap before planning more activity
insights.evidence: 2026/27 national non-devolved ASF grant · illustration: on a £1m allocation, a 97% threshold is £970,000. Eligible delivery of £950,000 leaves a £20,000 gap to that threshold.
insights.meaning: This is a delivery gap, not a repayment estimate. The authority allocation table is not your provider agreement; devolved and procured arrangements need their own rules.
insights.action: Reconcile forecast ILR, EAS and funding-claim values to the relevant agreement and eligible funding lines. Use the planning tool to establish the gap before deciding what additional delivery can close it.

insights.title: Extra activity may not count towards the funding threshold
insights.evidence: 2026/27 national non-devolved ASF grant · section 3.3: tailored learning and innovative provision count only up to agreement values. Funding above the overall allocation is conditional.
insights.meaning: More delivery on a capped line may add cost without reducing the reconciliation gap. Funding up to 110% is subject to affordability and track-record checks, not an automatic entitlement.
insights.action: Identify which eligible funding line an additional cohort would earn against and whether its cap has been reached. Confirm the funding basis before committing expenditure; apply the relevant local rules to devolved delivery.

rules.title: Respect devolution
rules.text: National non-devolved rules do not replace each authority’s rules. Hull and East Yorkshire, for example, specifies its own resident scope and evidence requirements.

rules.title: Apply tolerance narrowly
rules.text: The 97% reconciliation threshold shown here applies to the national grant arrangement in section 3.3, not universally to procured or devolved contracts.

rules.title: Check the learner and funding line before enrolment
rules.text: For national non-devolved ASF, the learner’s permanent residence immediately before enrolment determines the funding route. Match the postcode, eligibility evidence, learning aim and funding year to the agreement. A devolved allocation does not authorise a provider to apply national rules to that authority’s learners.

rules.title: Cap the delivery included in reconciliation
rules.text: Section 3.3 counts tailored learning and innovative provision only up to the values in the national grant agreement when assessing 97% delivery. Funding above contract value is subject to affordability and conditions, not guaranteed income. The calculator is a planning illustration; the reconciliation statement determines repayment.

rules.title: Keep allocation scope and funding years separate
rules.text: The selected S31 authority allocations are April–March financial-year figures, not provider August–July agreement values. Keep core ASF and other funding streams distinct; adding parent allocations to their components double-counts funding.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Replaced generic funding cautions with a conditional reconciliation example and a funding-line decision. National grant rules are not applied to devolved or procured agreements.

gaps: This 13-authority S31 table excludes Integrated Settlement authorities and national provider allocations.
No public, current provider earnings series is joined to allocations. Other local rulebooks require individual review.

programmes.name: Sector-based Work Academy Programme
programmes.period: Starts to June 2026; earnings to April 2026

insights.title: The new ambition is 18.4% above last year’s delivery
insights.evidence: England & Scotland · the 2026/27 target is 115,000 starts, against 97,130 recorded in 2025/26: approximately 17,870 additional starts, or 18.4% growth.
insights.meaning: This is a larger expansion than comparing the two annual targets suggests. Apr–Jun 2026 starts of 28,490 represent 24.8% of the target, but do not establish a full-year forecast or a provider allocation.
insights.action: Test proposed cohort volumes against named employer vacancies, placement capacity and guaranteed interview commitments. Resolve any shortfall with employer and Jobcentre partners before committing training places.

insights.title: The latest matched earnings observation is lower
insights.evidence: Linked UC starters · 35.8% of the Oct 2025 cohort had earnings six months later, compared with 37.9% for Oct 2024 at the same horizon: 2.1 percentage points lower.
insights.meaning: Equivalent start months and follow-up periods make the comparison more useful. Different cohorts and labour-market conditions prevent a causal judgement; earnings in one month do not prove continuous work.
insights.action: Review local sector mix, interview-to-job conversion and continuing employer fit. Trace where participants leave the route to work before changing the cohort plan; do not apply the linked-UC rate to all starters.

rules.title: Connect training to real demand
rules.text: The employer guide describes pre-employment training, work experience, and a guaranteed interview or help with the employer’s recruitment process. Agree the actual vacancy and recruitment commitment with Jobcentre Plus before recruiting a cohort; do not promise a job.

rules.title: Use cohort timing and the correct population
rules.text: A start means beginning pre-employment training. Earnings are measured at six and nine months after the start for linked UC participants. Average earnings describe only those earning in that month.

rules.title: Agree the employer offer before starting a cohort
rules.text: SWAP can last up to six weeks and is available through Jobcentre Plus in England and Scotland, not Wales. Confirm training content, placement capacity, selection requirements and the interview or recruitment route with the employer. CareerPath recommends reviewing attendance, completion, interviews and sustained work separately.

rules.title: Find the local partnership contact
rules.text: The linked DWP directory gives Jobcentre Plus Service Leader contacts for local partnership discussions. It was updated on 15 September 2026. Use the relevant district to confirm the local SWAP route and employer demand; inclusion in the directory does not mean a commissioning opportunity is open.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Compared the new target with actual previous-year delivery and equivalent six-month earnings cohorts. Targets, provisional starts and linked-UC observations remain distinct.

gaps: Earnings observations cover starts linked to Universal Credit records, not all SWAP starts. No provider-level performance or causal impact estimate is presented.
Starts are provisional clerical MI, rounded to 10. Earnings data end in April 2026; later follow-up cells are not yet available. Unknown geography is retained.

programmes.name: Youth Guarantee Trailblazers

insights.title: Digital-only outreach may miss the intended young people
insights.evidence: Dudley · Year 1 learning in WMCA’s 2026/27 proposals identifies digital exclusion, low confidence and complex circumstances. Year 2 combines digital work with traditional outreach.
insights.meaning: An online response count may miss people who need contact through a trusted local organisation. This is local reported learning, not national prevalence or proof of the best-performing channel.
insights.action: Review engagement and first attendance by referral channel with community partners. Change the outreach mix where intended groups are absent, and follow accepted referrals through to attendance.

insights.title: School transitions and adult placements need different handovers
insights.evidence: West Midlands · 2026/27 proposals include proactive Year 11 enrolment alongside placement and transition support.
insights.meaning: A school destination and an adult work placement require different receiving teams and milestones. These are delivery plans, not achieved outcomes, and should not be reported as one undifferentiated referral total.
insights.action: Name the receiving school, college, apprenticeship or placement team for each route. Track a confirmed next destination and attendance, with consent and ownership agreed before the young person leaves the referring service.

insights.title: Match the support offer as well as age and postcode
insights.evidence: West of England directory · checked 20 Sep 2026: South Gloucestershire lists up to 20 weeks’ support and an eight-week coached placement; North Somerset has a care-experienced 18–21 offer.
insights.meaning: Similar programme labels cover different support intensity and intended groups. These are selected local examples; a published application route does not confirm that a place is available.
insights.action: Match the young person’s needs, location and age to the named offer. Confirm capacity, support duration and the receiving contact, then record whether the handover led to attendance.

rules.title: Track destinations consistently
rules.text: Separate engagement, learning entry, apprenticeship starts and sustained employment. Align definitions with the local agreement before comparison.

rules.title: West of England: route by local need
rules.text: The authority lists Bath & North East Somerset Council for rural transport barriers, South Gloucestershire Council for SEND or mental-health needs, and Bristol City Council for the South Bristol place-based cohort. Use the linked authority page to reach the Skills Connect youth directory and confirm current eligibility and intake before referral.

rules.title: Check status before describing a project as open
rules.text: West of England also lists North Somerset Council’s Opportunity South West for care-experienced 18–21-year-olds. Its UWE research project had a March 2026 completion date; that is not evidence of an open participant service in September. The local page is an example, not a national directory of live contracts.

rules.title: Local delivery · Birmingham
rules.text: 2026/27 proposal: Birmingham City Council links 18–21 support with NHS, anchor employers and community providers. Published enquiry route: YouthTrailblazer@birmingham.gov.uk. Confirm intake and eligibility before referral.

rules.title: Local delivery · Dudley
rules.text: 2026/27 proposal: ICAN plans 40 three-month paid placements with Dudley Council, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust and employers. This is a target. The linked authority page gives the local enquiry contact.

rules.title: Local delivery · Wolverhampton
rules.text: 2026/27 proposal: Open Door offers a 4–12-week placement model for 18–21-year-olds, linked with Wolves at Work and Connexions. Use the authority’s named contact to confirm current access.

rules.title: Local delivery · South Bristol
rules.text: Directory listing: 16–21-year-olds in South Bristol, including BS3, BS4, BS13 and BS14. Career coaching, work tasters and wellbeing support; apply through the South Bristol form linked by Skills Connect.

rules.title: Local delivery · South Gloucestershire
rules.text: Directory listing: ages 16–21, including SEND or mental-health needs. Up to 20 weeks’ support and an eight-week coached placement. Skills Connect provides the application route; confirm available places.

rules.title: Local delivery · North Somerset care leavers
rules.text: Directory listing: care-experienced 18–21-year-olds; specialist coaching and help with work barriers. Use the care-leaver application link on Skills Connect. Current capacity and the individual service end date are not published here.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Used Dudley outreach learning, West Midlands transition plans and specific West of England support offers to improve referral decisions. Local proposals are not national results.

gaps: The published research describes design and early implementation, not current performance.
Local delivery targets, spend and outcomes need current authority evidence and agreement-level definitions.

Local delivery examples cover West Midlands and West of England only. The eight-area research matrix is not a national directory of open services. Application links are published routes, not confirmed places; local outcome rates and exact service end dates remain unverified.
matrix: Care experience; risk of long-term NEET
NEET or at risk; additional barriers
Hidden NEET; transition and mental-health needs

programmes.name: Economic Inactivity Trailblazers

insights.title: For carers, the hours can matter before the vacancy
insights.evidence: North East · Nov 2025–Jan 2026 research, Figure 8: 65% of economically inactive carer respondents identified finding work that fits caring responsibilities as a barrier. The question had 184 carer respondents.
insights.meaning: A vacancy match can fail if hours and caring commitments are incompatible. This is a local self-reported sample, not a national estimate or evidence of programme impact.
insights.action: Establish workable hours, flexibility and reliable care arrangements before proposing a vacancy. Agree those conditions with the employer and the carer, then record whether the offer is workable in practice.

insights.title: Turn a named partner into a confirmed handover
insights.evidence: North East · authority page updated 11 Sep 2026: named 2026/27 services cover youth, neurodiversity and primary-care routes. The overall project status is still “Mobilising”.
insights.meaning: A partner appointment does not confirm that a specific intake is open; equally, the overall status does not prove every service is closed. Referral decisions need service-level confirmation.
insights.action: Use the listed partner for the relevant support need. Confirm eligibility, capacity, start/end dates and who accepts the handover; track accepted referrals separately from enquiries and follow through to attendance.

rules.title: Keep evaluation context
rules.text: The June 2026 research reports fieldwork from 2025. Refresh local implementation evidence before calling an intervention current.

rules.title: Turn the funding map into a local delivery check
rules.text: Start with the named funding recipient and ask for the current delivery partner, postcode and cohort eligibility, referral route, service start/end dates and outcome definitions. CareerPath recommends recording engagement, progression and sustained work separately. An allocation announcement alone does not establish an open contract or participant service.

rules.title: Local delivery · North East youth pathways
rules.text: 2026/27 appointed partners: Groundwork NE & Cumbria (Northern Futures) and Newcastle United Foundation (North East Connected). The authority page lists their contacts; age limits and open intake need confirmation.

rules.title: Local delivery · North East neurodiversity
rules.text: 2026/27 appointed partner: North East Autism Society, Neurodiversity Employment Service NE. Use its contact in the authority directory to confirm eligibility and referral arrangements.

rules.title: Local delivery · North East primary care
rules.text: 2026/27 appointed partners: First Contact Clinical (First Contact to Purpose) and Recovery Connections (LIFT OFF!). Confirm the health-to-employment handover with the listed project contact.

rules.title: Funding and impact have different units
rules.text: The £80m announcement has seven funding recipients covering nine trailblazer areas. The GLA’s £20m is shared across three areas. Allocation is not expenditure, and regional inactivity changes cannot establish the impact of an individual intervention.

rules.title: Review update · 20 September 2026
rules.text: Added North East carers research on work fitting caring responsibilities and strengthened named-partner handovers. The survey sample and mobilisation status are explicit.

gaps: Comparable current local output and outcome series are not verified.
Allocation is not expenditure; programme impact requires evaluation evidence.

Named 2026/27 partners are currently shown for the North East only. Exact service dates, open referral capacity and comparable local outcome rates are not verified. Other trailblazer areas retain funding and research evidence; no national delivery directory is claimed.

The carers finding is local research with 184 carer respondents to the specific barriers question. It is not a representative population estimate. Fieldwork was November 2025–January 2026. The exact publication date has not been confirmed.
